title: Enhancing Water and Sanitation Through Innovation and Collaboration Amid Global Conflicts: A Perspective on Sustainable Development Goal 6
content:
ABSTRACT

This article is a “Perspective” piece, synthesizing and interpreting existing literature to offer a viewpoint on the challenges and opportunities related to SDG 6. Failure to advance toward Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6)—universal access to safe water and sanitation—threatens global public health, safety, and socioeconomic development. Without progress, communities face higher risks of waterborne diseases, reduced quality of life, and limited educational and economic opportunities, especially for vulnerable groups. Meeting SDG 6 requires increased investment, innovation, and collaboration. However, this perspective argues that global conflicts, exacerbated by contemporary geopolitical dimensions of globalization, are a primary barrier to progress. These conflicts obstruct SDG 6 by disrupting water supply chains, destroying infrastructure, and diverting resources from crucial projects. We systematically review the evidence quantifying the impacts of conflict on water and sanitation, demonstrating that conflict-affected countries have, on average, 20% lower rates of access to safely managed drinking water than stable countries. We explore innovative technological solutions and sustainable practices, such as smart water management, water recycling, and nature-based solutions, alongside successful collaborative case studies from post-conflict Rwanda, Singapore, India, and China. We also address the specific challenges of implementing water technologies in conflict-affected settings and recommend conflict-sensitive, low-tech solutions where appropriate. We conclude that peace is not merely a parallel goal but an essential prerequisite for effective resource allocation and the successful implementation of water and sanitation solutions. While progress can occur even in the absence of complete peace, a stable and cooperative international environment is critical for accelerating progress toward SDG 6, ensuring that improvements in water and sanitation contribute to broader objectives of health, equality, and economic prosperity.
